sentences.text: The pill organizer has fourteen compartments now; I dream about the little plastic lids clicking shut. It took forty years to walk through that door, and now she wants me back on Thursday like it's nothing. Three hours at the pharmacy arguing about a prior authorization, then home to reheat a dinner nobody remembered wanting. Who did I used to be before every conversation became about swallowing, toileting, and what got forgotten today? Mom asked me what day it was eleven times before breakfast, and I answered all eleven like it was the first. She asked what brought me in, and I heard myself say "nothing, really," which we both knew was a lie. Tuesday at four, she said, same time next week — and I nodded like a person who knows where I'll be next week. There's a smell to this house now — pill bottles, lavender wipes, something underneath I've stopped trying to name. Nobody warns you that grief can start while the person is still sitting at your kitchen table. Two buses and a fifteen-minute walk each way, every single week — I keep wondering if I can actually sustain that. He asked me who I was tonight, politely, the way you'd ask a stranger holding your coat. In July my sister promised she'd take a weekend; it's October now and I've stopped asking. She calls me by her sister's name most evenings, and correcting her stopped feeling worth it around Easter. Filling out the intake form took longer than the crying did. Three weeks until the next opening, the coordinator said, and I laughed a little, because what else. When I finally said the ugly thing out loud, she didn't flinch, and her not flinching undid something in me. Sometimes I lock the bathroom door and run the fan, just to buy ninety seconds no one can interrupt. Fragile isn't the word; scraped clean is closer to how the drive home felt. Cancelled my own doctor's appointment twice this month because there was no one to sit with her. When did I last sleep through a whole night without listening for the door alarm? I want to write a suicide letter.
